questions.question_text: A rectangular prism measures $7$ cm long, $4$ cm wide and $3$ cm high. Calculate its surface area.

options.why: Found the volume $7\times4\times3$ instead of the surface area.
Added one of each face but forgot that faces come in matching pairs.
Left out the top and bottom pair of faces.

questions.solution_text:
$A_1 = (7\times 3)\times 2$
$= 42\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = (4\times 3)\times 2$
$= 24\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = (7\times 4)\times 2$
$= 56\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3$
$= 122\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: Calculate the surface area of a cube with side length $4$ cm.

options.why: Cubed the side ($4^{3}$), which is the volume, not the surface area.
Found the area of only one face.
Multiplied the side by $6$ instead of the area of a face by $6$.

questions.solution_text:
A cube has $6$ identical square faces.
$\text{SA} = 6\times 4^{2}$
$= 6\times 16$
$= 96\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A triangular prism has a right-angled cross-section with sides $9$ cm, $12$ cm and $15$ cm, and is $8$ cm long. Calculate its surface area.

options.why: Counted only one triangular end instead of two.
Left out the two triangular end faces entirely.
Did not halve base $\times$ height for the triangular faces.

questions.question_text: A triangular prism has a right-angled cross-section whose two shorter sides are $8$ cm and $15$ cm. The prism is $5$ cm long. Calculate its surface area.

options.why: Added the two legs ($8+15$) to get the third side instead of using Pythagoras.
Used a leg length for the sloping rectangle instead of the hypotenuse.
Counted only one triangular end instead of two.

questions.question_text: A triangular prism has a right-angled cross-section. Its longest side is $13$ cm and one shorter side is $5$ cm. The prism is $7$ cm long. Calculate its surface area.

options.why: Did not halve base $\times$ height for the triangular faces.
Counted only one triangular end instead of two.
Left out the two triangular end faces entirely.

questions.solution_text:
The missing side is shorter than the hypotenuse, so subtract inside Pythagoras' theorem.
$x^{2} = 13^{2} - 5^{2}$
$= 144$
$x = 12\text{ cm}$
$A_1 = 2\times\frac{1}{2}\times 5\times 12$
$= 60\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = 5\times 7$
$= 35\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = 12\times 7$
$= 84\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_4 = 13\times 7$
$= 91\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3 + A_4$
$= 270\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: An open-topped box has a rectangular base $8$ cm by $5$ cm and a height of $4$ cm. Calculate the total area of its five faces.

options.why: Included the missing top face, treating the box as closed.
Left out the base as well as the top.
Found only the area of the base.

questions.solution_text:
The box has no top face, so add the base and the four sides.
$A_1 = 8\times 5$
$= 40\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_2 = (8\times 4)\times 2$
$= 64\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_3 = (5\times 4)\times 2$
$= 40\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{SA} = A_1 + A_2 + A_3$
$= 144\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A trough is a trapezoidal prism. Its trapezium cross-section has parallel sides $14$ cm and $8$ cm, a height of $4$ cm, and two sloping sides of $5$ cm each. The prism is $10$ cm long. Calculate its surface area.

options.why: Counted only one trapezium end instead of two.
Left out the two trapezium end faces entirely.
Did not halve $(a+b)h$ for the trapezium faces.

questions.question_text: A rectangular prism has a base $12$ cm by $4$ cm and a height of $x$ cm. Its surface area is $256\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find the value of $x$.

options.why: Left out the two $12$ by $4$ end faces and solved $32x=256$.
Did not double the four side faces, solving $96+16x=256$.
Added $96$ instead of subtracting it, solving $32x=352$.
